title: How Agile and Scrum really work, and when to use Kanban

say: How Agile and Scrum really work, and when to use Kanban.
This is the video for module 1 of Agile and Scrum in Practice.

Picture a team building a school fees portal in Abuja. In a plan-driven project, often called waterfall, they gather every requirement first, build for months, and test at the end. The school owners see nothing usable until month six.
An Agile team works in short cycles of 1 to 4 weeks. Each cycle ends with a small working piece that real users can try. They collect feedback and adjust the plan.
Agile does not mean no plan. Both approaches plan. The difference is how often the plan meets reality.
The team assumed parents would pay by card. Most actually pay by bank transfer or USSD.

card.title: The cost of a late discovery

say: With 4 developers at about 25,000 naira a day, the team costs 100,000 naira a day.

card.title: The cost of a late discovery

say: In waterfall, the error appears in testing after 60 days. 30% of the work depends on it, so 18 days must be redone. That is 1,800,000 naira.

card.title: The cost of a late discovery

say: In Agile, parents try the first payment screen after sprint 1. Only about 3 days of work depend on the wrong idea. That is 300,000 naira.
One sixth of the cost, and about two months of delay avoided. That is the core argument for short cycles: inspect what really happened, then adapt.

say: Scrum is the most used framework for putting Agile to work. It is defined in the free Scrum Guide, last updated in November 2020. A Scrum Team is typically 10 or fewer people, with three accountabilities.
The Product Owner is one person, not a committee. She maximises value and orders the Product Backlog.

cards.d: One person, not a committee. Maximises value and orders the Product Backlog.
A leader who serves: coaches, facilitates, removes blockers. Not a task manager.
Create a usable Increment every Sprint. Testers, designers and writers count too.

say: The Scrum Master is a leader who serves. She coaches and removes blockers. A common mistake is acting as a task manager who assigns work.

cards.d: One person, not a committee. Maximises value and orders the Product Backlog.
A leader who serves: coaches, facilitates, removes blockers. Not a task manager.
Create a usable Increment every Sprint. Testers, designers and writers count too.

say: The Developers create a usable Increment every Sprint. Developer does not mean only programmers. Testers, designers and writers are Developers too.

say: A timebox is a maximum duration. The Sprint holds all the other events. Many teams use 2 weeks, which is 10 working days.
Sprint Planning decides why this Sprint is valuable and what can be done. About 4 hours for 2 weeks.
The Daily Scrum is 15 minutes every working day. Developers check progress toward the Sprint Goal and adjust the plan.
The Sprint Review inspects the result with stakeholders, and the Retrospective plans how to work better.
For example, Amaka's team spends 10 hours per person on events out of about 80. That is 12.5%. Useful when a manager asks, why so many meetings?
Kanban has no Sprints and no fixed roles. First, show the work on a board with columns like To do, Doing, Review, Done.

panel.heading: Kanban in four practices
items: Visualise the work on a board

say: Second, limit work in progress. For example, no more than 3 cards in Doing. When the column is full, finish something first.

panel.heading: Kanban in four practices
items: Visualise the work on a board
panel.rule: When Doing is full, finish something before starting more.

say: Third, measure flow. Little's Law says cycle time equals work in progress divided by throughput.
For example, Funmi's support team has 30 tickets open and closes 10 a day. That is 3 days per ticket. She limits open tickets to 15, so each started ticket takes 1.5 days.

panel.heading: Kanban in four practices
items: Visualise the work on a board
panel.rule: When Doing is full, finish something before starting more.

say: Fourth, review the board and remove bottlenecks. But if 20 tickets arrive a day and only 10 close, no limit can hide that. Have an honest capacity conversation.

panel.heading: Kanban in four practices
items: Visualise the work on a board
panel.rule: When Doing is full, finish something before starting more.

say: Match the approach to the work. A new app suits Scrum, because the solution is uncertain. A help desk suits Kanban, because work arrives every hour.
A borehole to a known design suits a fixed plan. Campaigns plus urgent requests suit a hybrid.
If urgent work broke the plan almost every week last month, choose Kanban or keep capacity free.

panel.heading: Which approach fits the work?
items: Borehole to a known design: plan-driven

say: To remember. Agile means small working pieces, checked with real users often. Late discovery costs far more than early.
Scrum has a Product Owner, a Scrum Master and Developers. The Daily Scrum is 15 minutes. And lower work in progress means faster finishing.

panel.heading: Remember
items: Agile means small working pieces, checked often
Late discovery costs far more than early
Cycle time = work in progress ÷ throughput

say: Your tasks: spot a late discovery in a project you know, build a Sprint calendar and count the event hours, and diagnose three kinds of work with Little's Law.
